findings.breaking_input: arc-run.mjs --process no-such-process, or any process whose canonical file is missing or unparsed, so `doc` is null or undefined, run from a tree where the earlier `doc && ...job_stub` guard let execution continue.
findings.why: The earlier job_stub check is written `doc && Object.prototype...`, which implies `doc` can be falsy at this point. The new block calls `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(doc, "role")` with no guard, and `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(null, ...)` throws a TypeError. The result is a stack trace and a nonzero exit code that is not the documented operator-error 2, raised before routing and before any receipt.
findings.fix: Guard with `doc && typeof doc === "object" && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(doc, "role")`. If `doc` is falsy, return null and let the existing missing-process path report it.

findings.breaking_input: cd /elsewhere && org-judge.mjs --root ../arc --spine-dir ../spine --head H --receipt ULID --verdict accept --reason ok (relative --root or --spine-dir, cwd different from root).
findings.why: The receipt, placements and dedupe are read with paths resolved against the process cwd. The emit child is spawned with `cwd: root`, `arcEvent` is the relative path `join(root, ...)`, and `ARC_SPINE_ROOT` is the relative `spineDir`. Both resolve a second time against `root`, so the child either cannot find arc-event.mjs or writes to `root/<spineDir>`, a different spine from the one judged. That is the B1 read-here, write-there defect again, reached through relative paths. The earlier fix passed the env var but did not make it absolute.
findings.fix: After parsing, set `root = resolve(o.root)` and `spineDir = resolve(spineDir)` before any use. Pass only absolute paths to the emit child.
findings.twin_of: org-dispatch read governance and open proposals from `--spine-dir` but `--emit` wrote to the canonical spine, so the cap and dedupe counted a different spine than the writes

findings.breaking_input: org/teams/con.team.yaml as a regular file on a Windows checkout, or a directory or symlink named x.team.yaml.
findings.why: `teamStems` turns a directory listing straight into stems with no isFile or lstat check and no device-name or grammar check on the stem. `readTeam(root, stem)` then opens whatever the listing returned. This is the pattern already fixed for /api/org, not applied here.
findings.fix: Filter stems with lstat().isFile(), the stem grammar and the device-name exclusion before reading. Skip a link or directory, as the route does.
findings.twin_of: /api/org opened every `*.team.yaml` the listing returned, including `con.team.yaml` and a directory or symlink with that name

findings.breaking_input: Run --dry-run at 23:59 UTC and apply with the printed --expect after 00:00 UTC.
findings.why: The date comes from `new Date().toISOString()` and is written into the card's history line, which is part of the planned file content. The plan digest therefore changes across UTC midnight, and a correct apply is refused as stale. The date is also UTC while the lane records IST dates, so the history entry can be a day off the owner's calendar.
findings.fix: Take the date from the dry-run's own digest input, for example an optional --date, or use a date-free history line. Alternatively fix the date once and carry it in the printed expect token.

findings.breaking_input: skill-import.mjs github:acme/kit/clean-notes/SKILL.md@<sha> --role technical-writer --source fake --expect DIGEST, run on the owner's real clone.
findings.why: A fixture read from the repo's own tests/fixtures tree is allowed to pass the full apply path. It writes a real proposal branch and a real approval.requested receipt. That receipt carries the vetted-bytes digest and a source line that claims `github:acme/kit/...@sha`, though no GitHub fetch happened. Provenance is then forged by the tool's own test mode.
findings.fix: Refuse `--source fake` unless `--dry-run` is given or an explicit test env var is set. Alternatively write `fetched via: fake fixture` into the approval payload and the commit message.
